findings.title: Single-bit comparison result can be faulted from digest mismatch to valid ROM
findings.location: matches_q/matches_d digest comparison and prim_mubi4_sender good_o generation (approximately lines 130-166)
findings.description: The security decision is accumulated in the single-bit register matches_q, initialized to 1 and updated as matches_q && (digest_word == exp_digest_word). The subsequent MuBi sender only encodes this one-bit decision; it does not independently verify it. A targeted bit upset that changes matches_q from 0 to 1 after a mismatching digest word, or while the comparator is in its terminal Done state, causes good_o to become a valid MuBi4True encoding. Likewise, a transient fault forcing the sole 32-bit equality result high during the mismatching word prevents matches_q from clearing. The sparse comparator FSM and redundant address counter do not detect either fault. An attacker able to alter a ROM word and inject a timed fault during boot can therefore make the power manager observe a successful ROM check and permit execution of modified immutable code. Forwarding the computed digest to key manager does not restore the ROM execution-integrity decision and may only perturb downstream key derivation.
findings.recommendation: Implement the digest acceptance decision with independent redundancy rather than merely MuBi-encoding a single result. For example, compare the full digest twice using independently preserved logic and different word order or control, maintain redundant fail-sticky state using complementary or sparse encoding, and raise a fatal alert on disagreement or invalid encoding. Generate good_o only when both independent checks explicitly report a match. Ensure that once either checker records a mismatch, no normal transition or single-bit state upset can restore a successful result before reset.
